title: NORTH WAYNE SCHOOL BOARD
full_story:
The North Wayne School Board met in regular session Wednesday night and got an update from Todd Cyrulik with BLDD architectural firm on a potential district restructuring plan.

The Board approved an overnight trip for FCCLA to Evansville, on July 27th and 28th, and the renewal for employee health insurance through the Egyptian Trust.  They also set the 26-27 fees as follows; drivers ed fees $50, registration fees $40, community use of facilities $50 for Johnsonville or Mt. Erie and $75 for CHS or CMS, admission to athletic events $3, adult lunches $3.70, adult breakfasts $1.55, and extra milk $.50.

In personnel action the board accepted a letter of resignation from Nick Howard as CHS Assistant Baseball Coach, and hired Misty Ellis as CHS Assistant Softball coach.

title: CCH SPORTS PHYSICALS
full_story:
The Clay County Hospital is offering free sports physicals for the next school year.

The first opportunity for a free sports physical is on Wednesday at the Clay City Clinic.  The next happens on Wednesday, July 8th at the Flora Clinic, then Wednesday July 9th at the Louisville Clinic and finally Tuesday, July 14th at the Flora Clinic.  All clinics are from 4 to 6 pm.  Wabash General Hospital athletic trainers will be at the clinics to assess athlete’s injury risk.

Appointments are not needed; physicals will be done on a first-come first-serve basis.  Sports physicals do not qualify as school physicals.

title: CLAY COUNTY MOBILE HOME TAXES
full_story:
The 2026 Mobile Home Privilege Tax Bills were mailed out on Monday, April 20th.  The due date for mobile home taxes is coming up on July 1st, but you can pay the taxes at any time.  After July 1st, you will be charged an additional $25.00 per month.

If you did not receive a mobile home Privilege tax bill, and you own a mobile home, please contact the Treasurer’s office immediately at 618-665-3727 or email [email protected].

Clay County taxpayers can pay their mobile home taxes by mail by sending their check with the payment stub to the Clay County Treasurer PO Box 88 Louisville 62858.  Mailed payments must be postmarked on or before the due date to avoid penalty.  Mobile home privilege tax bills can be paid at the Treasurer’s office in the Clay County Courthouse, they accept cash, check, cashier’s check, or money orders.  Please bring your entire bill if you want it stamped to show proof of payment.  The Clay County Treasurer’s office hours are from 8 am to 4 pm and they are open during the noon hour.  Payment can be made by placing payment in the envelope depository at the north entrance of the Clay County Courthouse.  Please include payment stub.  Tax Bills can also be paid online by credit/debit card by going to govpaynow.com PLC number a00082.

title: S.U.R.E. SYMPOSIUM
full_story:
The Clay County Health Department is collaborating with the Coalition Against Drug Abuse of Clay County, the Clay County Board, SIU School of Medicine, and Birth to Five Illinois to bring the second Substance Use Resource & Education Symposium or S.U.R.E Symposium to Clay County on August 11th.  Registration will begin at 8:30 am at the Oil Belt Christian Service Camp.

The goal of the S.U.R.E. Symposium is to bring together local agencies, experts, and community members to provide a safe space to learn about substance abuse prevention, recovery, and what happens after.

Lunch will be provided to the first 200 who register, and continuing education units are pending.  Register by going to tinyurl.com/SURE2026 or use the QR code on the health department’s website.  This years symposium registration is being covered by the Clay County Board Opioid Settlement.

title: SUMMER FOOD SERVICE PROGRAM
full_story:
The Clay County Health Department’s Beyond the Bell program is participating in the Summer Food Service Program this summer.  Free meals, which meet Summer Food Service Program federal guidelines, are available to all children 18 years of age and under and to persons over 18 years of age who are enrolled in a state approved educational program for the mentally or physically disabled.

Free meals will be provided at the Beyond the Bell program through August 13th.

Breakfast will be served at Beyond the Bell to program participants from 8:00 to 9:00 am and lunch will be served from 11:30 am to 12:00 pm.  Menus for both meals will be posted on Beyond the Bell’s Facebook page.

Clay County Health Department, the program sponsor, is located at 601 E. 12th Street in Flora.  For further information, contact Tamara Byers or Kathryn Holstlaw at 618-662-8322.

The Food Distribution Program is available to all eligible participants without regard to race, color, national origin, age, sex, or handicap.  Any person who believes that he or she has been discriminated against in any USDA-related activity should write immediately to the Secretary of Agriculture, Washington, DC 20250, or call toll free (866) 632-9992 (Voice).  Individuals who are hearing impaired or have speech disabilities may contact USDA through the Federal Relay Service at (800) 877-8339 or (800) 845-6136 (Spanish).  USDA is an equal opportunity provider and employer.

title: SHOT CLOCK VOTE
full_story:
The Illinois High School Association (IHSA) Board of Directors met for its regularly scheduled meeting Monday, where the Board finalized expectations for the 35-second shot clock, which will be required for varsity boys and girls basketball contests beginning with the 2026-27 IHSA season.

“It is important that we provide clearcut guidelines to our schools on the expectations for the shot clock as we move toward the 2026-27 season,” said IHSA Executive Director Craig Anderson.  “We believe our Board was forward-thinking in providing significant planning time for schools to prepare for the shot clock.  It is imperative that all schools are afforded the same competitive experience and that every student-athlete competes under consistent conditions.  By establishing these expectations, schools have had ample opportunity to budget, plan, and install the necessary equipment, ensuring an equitable environment.”

The Board voted to accept the recommendation of the IHSA Basketball Advisory Committee by adding State Association Adoption #4, which reads “A school may not host a varsity contest if a shot clock is not installed or is not properly mounted on the backboard in the primary gym in accordance with NFHS rules.  The host school must secure an alternate facility or allow the opponent to host the contest.  If the host school is unable to secure a gym with functioning shot clocks and the opposing school cannot host, the game shall be forfeited by the home team.”

Additionally, State Association Adoption #4 addresses events that use multiple-gyms: “When a school hosts a tournament or shootout utilizing multiple gyms or sites, and a traditional backboard-mounted shot clock is not feasible in an auxiliary gym, shot clocks must be mounted on the wall behind the basket, at or above the backboard, and must be clearly visible and unobstructed.”

title: GAS UTILITY CONSTRUCTION BOOTCAMP
full_story:
Wabash Valley College will host a new Gas Utility Construction Bootcamp, a hands-on training program designed to prepare students for entry-level careers in the natural gas utility and pipeline construction industry.  The bootcamp runs Monday, August 3rd through 14th.

The intensive 2-week course will be held from 8 am to 6 pm at the WVC campus in Mt. Carmel, offering 90 hours of expert training in gas main and service installation, safety protocols, and readiness for Department of Transportation Operator Qualifications (OQ).

Class size is limited to 10 students.  The full bootcamp investment is $1,200, which includes industry-recognized certifications and job placement support.

Applicants must attend all sessions, pass a background check and drug screening, maintain a clean driving record, and be willing to travel or relocate for job opportunities.

People who want to apply for the program can visit https://iecc.edu/gas-utility.

title: GRAND LEVEE JUNE 20th
full_story:
The Vandalia Statehouse State Historic Site will host the annual Grand Levee, a celebration of the grand receptions held during the 1800s to honor government dignitaries and important visitors, tomorrow.

The event, featuring an entire day of activities and entertainment, is free and open to the public.  The historic site is at 315 West Gallatin Street in Vandalia.

Festivities will begin at 10 am tomorrow on the lawn of the Vandalia Statehouse with period arts and crafts demonstrations, children’s activities, painting and woodcarving by the Fayette County Art Connection, and performances by the Dulcimer Guy.  Food and beverages will be available for purchase, and the Rotary Club will provide free funnel cakes.

Other activities include performances by the Clockwork Clown, Times in History: A Traveling Museum, Professor Farquar and Polecat Annie, and the Singing Blacksmith Bryan Dale Headley.  Families can enjoy giant bubble activities with Wild Foam Adventures and get up close with animals with the Lucky R Mobile Petting Zoo.

For a schedule of events and more information, visit the Vandalia Statehouse State Historic Site on Facebook or call 618-283-1161.

The Vandalia Statehouse is the oldest surviving capitol building in Illinois.  It served as the state capital from 1836 to 1839 and is open to the public between 9 am and 5 pm Wednesday through Sunday.

title: STATE UNEMPLOYMENT
full_story:
The Illinois Department of Employment Security (IDES) announced Thursday that the unemployment rate remained at 5.1% in May, unchanged from April, and up .7% of a point from the same month, one year ago, based on data provided by the US Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS).  The revised April unemployment rate was 5.1 percent.

Total nonfarm payrolls saw a third consecutive over-the-month increase in May, up 6,000, to 6,164,800.  The April monthly change in payrolls was up 11,400, unchanged from the preliminary report.  The May payroll jobs estimate and unemployment rate reflect activity for the week including the 12th.

The industry sectors with the largest monthly payroll jobs increases included: Trade, Transportation and Utilities up 2,700, Manufacturing up 2,300, and Government up 1,800.  The sectors with over-the-month jobs decreases included: Financial Activities down 3,300, and Other Services down 600.

Compared to a year ago, total nonfarm payroll jobs were down 2,300 jobs.  The industry groups with the largest jobs increases included: Private Education and Health Services up 18,800, Construction up 8,100 and Government up 4,300.  The industry groups with the largest jobs decreases included: Professional and Business Services down 17,900, Financial Activities down 11,800, and Trade, Transportation and Utilities down 6,200.  In May, total nonfarm payrolls were almost unchanged over-the-year in Illinois and up .3% percent in the nation.
